hero.tagline: Project management template for Claude Code
hero.description: One launcher, one command. Specialized agents, scoping tuned to each milestone, built-in GitHub — to ship your projects with quality and consistency.
problems.title: AI-assisted development lacks structure
problems.subtitle: Claude Code is powerful — but without a framework, every project starts from scratch.
problems.p1.title: Inconsistent workflows
problems.p1.desc: Every feature follows a different path. No standard, no systematic review, frequent gaps.
problems.p2.title: Lost context between sessions
problems.p2.desc: Claude doesn't remember the previous session. Version, decisions, project rules — everything gets repeated.
problems.p3.title: GitHub in silos
problems.p3.desc: Issues, milestones, PRs and releases managed manually, outside the development flow.
problems.p4.title: Tests written after the fact
problems.p4.desc: Tests arrive at the end of the cycle, poorly aligned with specs. Non-regression is never guaranteed.
workflow.title: CDP-orchestrated workflow
workflow.subtitle: Every command follows a precise pipeline, scoped per milestone. Agents work in parallel whenever possible, always validated at key checkpoints.
wf.plan.sub: 🧵 can delegate to sub-planner-N (independent issue groups)
wf.plan.team: 👥 re-evaluates the team: from the complete team defined at init, only the teammates the milestone needs
wf.gate2: Validate the plan, the scoping and the milestone team + alert BREAKING changes
wf.tests.desc: From plan + contracts · Unit / Integration / E2E · light: written by DEV
wf.review.desc: Quality · OWASP security · Contract coverage by tests · light: QA only
wf.qa.desc: Runs scripts · Follows manual procedures · Starts as soon as tests are ready
wf.qa.sub: 🧵 can delegate to sub-qa-<scope>, each isolated in a detached git worktree, on committed code
wf.reviewqa.note: By default, QA doesn't wait for the Review verdict — REJECTED cancels QA and sends it back to DEV. Falls back to sequential mode when risk is high (per plan).
wf.doc.desc: CHANGELOG · API docs if needed · DONE label applied
wf.qualif.desc: Infra validation · increments a · Smoke tests · Test URL · light or no QUALIF: validation on the local build
wf.docfinal.desc: Release notes · QA results · Indicative version — doesn't wait on the deploy
wf.qualifdoc.note: GATE 4 opens only once both STAGING and documentation are finished.
wf.lots.note: Milestone with batches: one batch at a time — QUALIF, validation (GATE LOT, only if an issue of the batch carries VALID-HUMAINE, otherwise auto-validated), push, green CI, batch issues closed, next batch. GATE 4 happens only once.
wf.gate4: Manual validation — the CDP presents a summary of the scenarios and opens the test procedure in Chrome
wf.gate4.ko: ✗ NO → label EN COURS → back to DEV
wf.prod.desc: Merge · Tag · CI monitored · success: release notes + milestone closing offered · failure: adaptive rollback → responsible agent
wf.marketing.desc: Draft generated from the milestone and CHANGELOG
wf.marketing.note: Doesn't depend on the deploy outcome — published only once the deploy succeeds AND you validate the draft.
wf.cycles: Correction cycles max 3: REVIEW refuses → DEV fixes → REVIEW only. TEST-WRITER re-triggered only if scope changes (BREAKING/CHANGED in contracts/CHANGELOG.md).
github.title: Native GitHub integration
github.subtitle: The CDP drives issues, milestones and labels through the deployer and the gh CLI, which carries out its orders — no manual commands.
github.labels.title: Issue lifecycle
github.labels.desc: Every phase transition updates the label automatically — set by the deployer with gh, on the team leader's order.
github.lv: Batch in QUALIF, awaiting your test
github.l6: CI green (or after your sign-off, your choice)
github.labels.reset: Correction cycle or GATE 4 rejection → reset to EN COURS.
github.milestone.title: Milestones
github.milestone.desc: Sprints as GitHub milestones. The due date marks the start of development, the description keeps the history: scoping, batch status, dated log. Closing offered after release to production.
github.m.f3: Closing offered after release to production
github.m.f4: Remaining issues: moved, closed or left pending
github.m.f5: History and scoping written to the milestone description at every transition
github.backlog.title: Backlog & workflow detection
versioning.title: Version management
versioning.subtitle: The GitHub milestone is the single source of truth: it fixes X.Y.Z for the whole cycle, no agent recomputes it.
versioning.cycle.title: Lifecycle of a version
versioning.cycle.desc: Format X.Y.Z.a in dev/staging, X.Y.Z in prod — a is just a build counter.
versioning.l2: STAGING deploy — a+1 on every build
versioning.note: X.Y.Z is fixed once and for all by the milestone title — never recomputed mid-cycle.
versioning.semver.title: When to bump (SemVer)
versioning.semver.desc: Decided when the milestone is created, not after the fact.
versioning.minor: New feature, new agent, new command
versioning.patch: Bug fix, improvement to an existing template
versioning.tags.title: Tags & automated releases
versioning.tags.desc: The tag triggers CI — no manual release.
versioning.tags.note: Publishes the GitHub Release and updates the CHANGELOG, with no manual step.
features.title: Features
features.f1.title: Native TDD
features.f1.desc: The test-writer starts in parallel with DEV, from the plan and contracts. Existing tests are immutable unless a change is documented in contracts/CHANGELOG.md.
features.f2.title: Contract-first
features.f2.desc: The planner creates API contracts before any development. The reviewer verifies test coverage. BREAKING changes flagged at GATE 2.
features.f3.title: Parallel agents
features.f3.desc: DEV ∥ TEST-WRITER simultaneously. Backend ∥ Frontend if independent. Automatic merge conflict resolution before REVIEW.
features.f4.title: Issues & Milestones
features.f4.desc: Labels updated as soon as the event happens (PLANNING → PLAN A VALIDER → PRET → EN COURS → EN REVIEW → EN QA → DONE → LOT A VALIDER → closed → A PUBLIER). BLOQUE (modifier) and ABANDONNE (terminal) statuses. At DONE: push, then the issue is closed only once CI is green. Milestone closing offered after release to production.
features.f5.title: A complete team, tailored to each milestone
features.f5.desc: At init, /init-project defines the project's complete skill team: PM, Planner, Dev (one or more instances per stack), Test-Writer, Reviewer, QA, Infra, Deployer, Doc, Security, PR-Reviewer, Marketing, plus generic business agents. Then, for each milestone, the team is re-evaluated: only the teammates that milestone needs are brought in — a light patch doesn't spin up the whole team.
features.f6.title: STAGING → PROD pipeline
features.f6.desc: Access and infra validation before every publish/deploy. Smoke tests. PROD deploy: CI is actively monitored — CODE/FLAKY failure → merge revert + tag deletion, CONFIG/INFRA failure → tag deletion only. The deployer reports facts to the teamleader, never fixes on its own. The release pipeline is audited if it exists, generated otherwise (infra contract C1-C11); the tag is the source of truth for the version, CI checks it without changing it.
features.f7.title: Session memory
features.f7.desc: Project memory is initialized by /init-project. /start-session reads project state, version, active milestone — and offers to resume an interrupted workflow (closed terminal) where it stopped. /end-session, fully delegated to agents, updates the memory.
features.f8.title: Auto-generated marketing site
features.f8.desc: /marketing generates this site from closed milestone issues, CHANGELOG and README. Dynamic version and roadmap from GitHub.
features.f9.title: CLAUDE.md maintained by the template
features.f9.desc: CLAUDE.md is split into two zones: Zone 1 (project config, agents, project-specific rules — never overwritten) and Zone 2 between BEGIN/END TEAMLEADER_PROTOCOL markers (multi-agent coordination protocol, replaced at each sync via awk). Loaded natively by Claude Code, coordination rules survive context compaction without any hook. A drift analysis detects gaps between template and deployed files at each sync.
features.f10.title: Agent lifecycle
features.f10.desc: Three spawn types. Core (planner, deployer): spawned at /start-session. Milestone (DEV agents, test-writer, code-reviewer, qa, doc-updater): only if the milestone scoping needs them, respawned on resume. One-off (security, infra, marketing): for the duration of a task. Between tasks agents stay IDLE; the CDP dispatches via SendMessage. Minimal protocol: ACTIF on receipt, DONE with a deliverable reference, back to IDLE. /team-status and /team-delete to monitor and close the team.
features.f11.title: Sub-agent delegation
features.f11.desc: planner, code-reviewer and qa can offload a large scope (issue groups, review dimensions, test scopes) to temporary sub-agents they drive directly, without going back through the CDP — which remains the sole spawner/closer. QA isolates each sub-agent in its own git worktree, created and cleaned up in Bash.
features.f12.title: Generic agents — non-dev projects
features.f12.desc: Not just code: /init-project can declare agents for business tasks (writing PowerPoint decks, documents, analyses). One shared template, one specification per instance (generic.<name>.md) — multiple instances allowed, each known to the CDP which dispatches it by role.
features.f13.title: Context audit at init
features.f13.desc: An init generates many files through substitution: /init-project ends with a state commit (return point) then /context-audit — unreplaced placeholders, broken references, inconsistencies between project-config.json, CLAUDE.md and agents. Automatic fixes are left to review in git diff. The same audit runs after a template sync.
features.f14.title: Controlled current branch
features.f14.desc: A single working branch at a time, set by the teamleader — the only one allowed to switch it or go back to a previous commit. Agents consume it: they check it at start and send a request to the teamleader for any other operation. A bugfix started during a milestone joins the plan with top priority and ships with it. Worktrees stay free, with no branch created, and tests only run on committed code.
features.f15.title: Live milestone panel
features.f15.desc: A Claude Code mod, reserved for the teamleader, shows on the right of the terminal the Claude account usage (session, week, per-model limits), then the issues of the current milestone, grouped by batch and phase, in GitHub label colors. Segmented progress bar, batches sorted by progress, 👤 on issues needing human validation, refreshed on every event.
features.f16.title: Batches delivered one at a time
features.f16.desc: The planner splits the milestone into independent batches (LOT-1, LOT-2.1…). One batch at a time: DEV, REVIEW, QA, then STAGING, your validation (GATE LOT), push, green CI, issues closed — then the next batch. Urgent release: ship the validated batches and move the rest to another milestone.
features.f17.title: States that say what is left to do
features.f17.desc: New PRET state: plan validated, development not started. Labels change as soon as the event happens — a teammate's return or a GATE validation — not only when the next order is sent: GitHub tracking reflects the real state.
features.f18.title: Model and effort per agent
features.f18.desc: The planner runs on fable (high effort), infra and the teamleader on opus, security on high, execution agents on medium, documentation on low. Each agent sets model and effort in its frontmatter, overridable per project; /init-project warns when a setting looks unsuited to the project.
features.f19.title: Pre-validation CI before tagging
features.f19.desc: A single CI script (CI_CMD) validated before it is written, a ci-branch.yml workflow that validates the branch without publishing anything, a barrier on the exact SHA before any PROD publish, and dedicated rules for unstable timing tests (FLAKY).
features.f20.title: Per-milestone scoping
features.f20.desc: Each milestone has its intensity: light or full, preset from the version type (patch, minor, major) and raised when an issue is breaking or security. The planner tunes the options (test-writer, review, QUALIF, documentation) and builds the team; you validate plan and scoping in a single question. Invariants never change: branch, versions, QA, green CI, human validation before production.
features.f21.title: Milestone history on GitHub
features.f21.desc: The milestone due date marks the start of development. Its description holds a scoping block, the status of each batch and a dated log (in progress, in QUALIF, rejected, released, closed) — updated by the deployer at every transition, readable directly on GitHub.
features.f22.title: Human or automatic validation
features.f22.desc: The test-writer tags each scenario AUTO (replayed by QA) or HUMAN. Only batches with a VALID-HUMAINE issue are submitted to you; at each GATE the CDP shows the summary and opens the test procedure in Chrome. GATE 4 before production is never skipped.
features.f23.title: Brief and environment access
features.f23.desc: /init-project scopes the product from a plain project description (or a guided workshop), searches the web for existing solutions, then collects and validates access to each environment (host, namespace, platform, region). Infra re-checks them before every publish or deploy.
features.f24.title: Agent and branch registry
features.f24.desc: The registry tracks the origin and version of every agent and shared context; a table at the end of init or sync shows which are up to date, pinned or behind, and when each is spawned. Leftover branches are classified (protected, safe, to review) and deleted on confirmation. Init ends with a publish to main.
features.f25.title: Containerized project, ready to go
features.f25.desc: With Claude-Launcher NG2 (≥ v5.5.0), a project runs in a container described by two files. .claude-launcher/env-template.yaml is generated by /init-project from your stack: packages, dependency install (npm ci, venv, Go or Node toolchain at the right version), re-run when a lock file changes, plus gh, jq and git access through gh. It is regenerated on every run and rewritten only when it changes. .claude-launcher/env.yaml stays yours: image, packages or steps specific to the project, never touched by the template. node_modules and .venv stay private to the container, so the host and other machines no longer clash.
features.f26.title: Close issues on your terms
features.f26.desc: By default, an issue closes as soon as QA passes and CI is green. If your team requires sign-off, pick it at init: the issue stays open (LOT A VALIDER or A PUBLIER while you decide) until you approve the batch or the milestone, before production.
features.f27.title: Fast tests
features.f27.desc: Agents run the tests related to what they change, not the whole suite; only QA replays everything, once per tree. /init-project spots a Windows toolchain used from WSL (several times slower) and switches to the Linux one.
features.f28.title: Private items kept safe
features.f28.desc: Keys, kubeconfigs, real data dumps, client documents: /init-project finds them and moves them to PRIVATE/, never committed. The list of what is expected is versioned, so a fresh clone knows what is missing.
features.f29.title: License chosen at init
features.f29.desc: /init-project detects the existing license or guides you to choose one (open source, proprietary, custom text), with holder and year, and creates the LICENSE file.
features.f30.title: Know when it's your turn
features.f30.desc: Three states say the team is waiting on you: PLAN A VALIDER (GATE 2), LOT A VALIDER (batch in QUALIF to test) and A PUBLIER (milestone ready for production). They show on issues, in the milestone state — even once every issue is closed — and in yellow in the milestone panel.
features.panel.caption: The milestone panel in the teamleader's terminal: three-state progress bar, batches sorted by progress, one line per issue.
install.title: Installation
install.subtitle: The tmux launcher manages all your projects from a central hub.
install.step1.title: Install Claude-Launcher NG2
install.step1.desc: A tmux hub that drives all your Claude Code projects, on the host or in a container:
install.lf1: Multi-project hub: laid-out teams, thumbnails, crash recovery
install.lf2: Containerized projects: podman, docker, ssh, Kubernetes
install.lf4: Refreshes init-project.md each time a project opens
install.v5note: Shared major version: template v5 goes with Claude-Launcher v5 (NG2). Close all projects before switching major versions.
install.step2.title: Configure and start
install.step2.desc: First run — creates the config, then launches the hub:
install.step3.title: Run /init-project
install.step3.intro: In Claude Code, type /init-project — two cases:
install.case1.title: New project
install.case1.desc: Scoping starts — from a brief or a guided interview:
install.case1.s1: Project brief or workshop: problem, audience, solution
install.case1.s2: Existing solutions searched on the web, docs/CADRAGE.md sheet
install.case1.s3: Tech stack, DEV agents, default milestone intensity
install.case1.s5: First milestone v0.1.0 and base issues
install.case1.s6: Generate CLAUDE.md + agents, publish to main, audit
install.case2.title: Existing project
install.case2.s1: v1/v2 → v3 migration; v3 → per-milestone scoping (v4)
install.case2.s3: .gitignore applied, clean commit published to main
install.case2.s4: Sync option to get new template features
working.title: Working on an existing project
working.subtitle: The typical cycle, from starting a session to shipping to production.
working.step1.title: Start the session
working.step1.desc: Claude reads the project state: current version, active milestone, work in progress.
working.step2.title: Scope the work
working.step2.desc: Create the target milestone, then the related issue — or search for an existing one in the backlog. At launch, the milestone gets its scoping, light or full.
working.step3.title: Develop
working.step3.desc: The CDP orchestrates the rest: plan and scoping validated together, then development, tests, review and QA according to the scoping.
working.step4.title: Validate
working.step4.desc: In QUALIF — or on the local build if the milestone has none — the CDP presents the scenarios to test: you confirm or send back to development.
working.step5.title: Ship to production
working.step5.desc: On validation, automatic deploy: merge, tag, monitored CI, release published, milestone updated.
working.step6.title: Close the session
working.step6.desc: Project memory updated, leftover branches cleaned on confirmation, teammates closed, session report generated.
commands.title: All commands
commands.subtitle: Every command triggers a specific agent or workflow.
commands.start-session: Starts the session: reads project memory, version and active milestone, spawns the core agents (and the current milestone's team), offers to resume an interrupted workflow, reports leftover branches
commands.end-session: Closes the session, fully delegated: git state and commit to the deployer, tests to qa, memory and docs to doc-updater; offers to delete safe leftover branches; closes teammates
commands.context-audit: Audits config files: duplicates, broken refs, drift between the template and deployed files — runs automatically at the end of /init-project
commands.init-project: Bootstraps a new project, migrates an older version, or syncs with the template
commands.feature: New feature — the CDP chains PLAN and scoping, DEV ∥ TEST-WRITER, REVIEW, QA, DOC then BUILD/QUALIF per the scoping, until your validation at GATE 4
commands.bugfix: Bug fix — same pipeline as /feature, with a mandatory regression test before review
commands.hotfix: Urgent production fix — direct deploy without waiting for STAGING, attached to the current active milestone
commands.refactor: Refactoring with no functional change — QA runs both before AND after to guarantee no regression
commands.backlog-search: Search an issue by keyword and automatically launch the workflow matching its label (feature, bug, hotfix…)
commands.milestone-new: Create a GitHub milestone and attach existing issues — no date: the due date is set when development starts
commands.milestone-status: Show the active milestone's progress (% bar, closed/open issues)
commands.milestone-close: Close the milestone — offers to move, close, or leave open any issues still unfinished
commands.progression: Real-time dashboard — status of every active agent in the team
commands.team-status: Team status, read-only: lists active teammates and their state (IDLE / EN COURS)
commands.team-delete: Closes IDLE teammates; with --force, closes all teammates, including those mid-task
commands.review: Runs a code review on the current diff, independently of the /feature pipeline
commands.qa: Runs test scripts and manual validation procedures, independently of the /feature pipeline
commands.secu: Full security audit: SAST, OWASP Top 10, vulnerable dependencies, exposed secrets
commands.build: Build a candidate version (no tests re-run) — local, environment-agnostic
commands.publish: Make the candidate available on an environment: promotion in QUALIF, merge + tag in PROD (deterministic rebuild by CI)
commands.deploy-qualif: Install in qualification the already published artifact, after access and infra validation, then smoke tests
commands.deploy-prod: Production deploy — if the version matches a milestone, triggers release communication prep in parallel; publishing only happens once the deploy succeeds AND you validate the draft
commands.marketing: Generates release notes and updates this site from the closed milestone and the CHANGELOG — auto-triggered by /deploy prod, or invocable on its own for a given version
roadmap.title: Roadmap
roadmap.source: Generated in real time from GitHub milestones and issues.
flow.title: Issue states
flow.subtitle: The GitHub label follows each workflow step, as soon as it happens. Yellow and purple: the ball is in your court; green: your decision.
flow.s.done: QA OK, batch deployed to QUALIF
flow.e.ask: GATE LOT: your test is expected
flow.s.avalider: Batch in QUALIF, awaiting your test
flow.back.title: Loops back
flow.back.1: Review rejected, QA failed or CI red → EN COURS.
flow.back.2: You reject: the issue at fault → EN COURS (fix) or PLANNING (scope revised); the others → DONE.
flow.back.3: Batch without VALID-HUMAINE: auto-validated, DONE → push directly, no LOT A VALIDER.
flow.mod.title: Modifiers
flow.mod.bloque: added on top of the phase, cause in a comment
flow.mod.human: a test scenario needs your judgment
github.lpub: Milestone ready for production, awaiting your Yes
flow.back.4: Issues already closed at GATE 4: the "⏸ to publish" wait is carried by the milestone state.
